error.message:
probes: passed → passed (passed)
Passed for dictation-style appends, one session-end cycle per field, both contexts (efs16d, spec of 17:12 JST): per field (Hospital Encounter, Important Points, pre-round editor; NH visit box, NH pre-round) the session ended on the server, the tail was appended, the sign-in prompt showed ('…code sent to your email'), a new code was entered, and every field held its first line + its own tail, no tail in another field. Hospital passed on its retry (first attempt: Encounter box not found within 20 s on the loaded stack); NH passed first time. NOT exercised: one session end across all fields (the scenario's 'when'); on main the app shows sign-in at the next server call (a tab switch is enough), so a physician cannot reach a second field after the session ends. The patch's oracleNote recording this scope change is PROPOSED for Quinn / Daniela's approval, not merged. History (tails typed key by key until 17:12 JST): efs16 4 attempts timed out on the loaded stack; efs16b + efs16c 7 attempts: 1 passed, 3 with tails missing after sign-in (NH visit x2, Hospital all three x1), 3 timeouts. Key-by-key typing is not a valid driver here: the app switches to sign-in at the first refused autosave and the remaining keys go to the sign-in screen, so only the text that was in the field at the switch exists to restore (a test artifact, not a loss).

descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT EFS state 10; TFA-94745 state 10, AC 3 · “Dictation kept; sign-in prompt; dictation available after signing back in”. Mixed: stated part — Sign-in prompt and each field's typed tail back after signing in; our part — Several fields at once with no tail landing in another field (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Approach · EFS Empty & Failure States · S16 Session ends mid-dictation in every autosave field, both contexts: sign-in prompt, and every tail is back in its own field after signing in

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U10a Session expired mid-dictation: the dictation is kept, a sign-in prompt shows, and the dictation is available after signing back in. (UAT EFS state 10; TFA-94745 state 10)
  • U13 Nothing the physician dictated or typed is lost in any failure state. (UAT EFS Expected Result; TFA-94745 AC 3)
  • U11 Every state shows a clear, plain-language message in the app's existing style that tells the physician what to do next (retry, enable permission, sign in, check connection). (UAT EFS Expected Result; TFA-94745 AC 1; TFA-94745 AC 5)
  • U14 Every state works in both Hospital and Nursing Home, on web, iOS and Android. (UAT EFS Expected Result; UAT 3.3; TFA-94745 AC 6)

Test design technique: State transition (state-transition) — Go through the steps in order (add → edit → delete, day 1 → day 2, offline → online) and check the state after each step.

Given Standard fixture; the harness ends the session on the server (sessions:_backdateForTests expiresAt = now − 1 s), never through the device clock

When Type a first line into each autosave field and let it save: Hospital Encounter box, Important Points and the pre-round notes editor; Nursing Home visit box and pre-round. The harness ends the session; type a tail into each field, ending with the Hospital pre-round editor left open; wait 3 s; …

Then A sign-in prompt shows; after signing in each field holds its first line and its own tail, and no tail appears in a different field

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): From U10a/U13: h1/n1 mustContain 'code sent to your email' (the sign-in prompt); every after-sign-in checkpoint mustContain its field's first line and tail. That each tail sits in its own field and in no other needs a field-value check in oracle.mjs (runnerGap); substring checks alone only prove the tail is on that screen. …

Where it ran: local probes (multi-device probes); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S16 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/EFS.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20 re-run), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane probes.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: probes.

The oracleNote that records this scope change is proposed for Quinn / Daniela's approval, not merged silently. Key-by-key typing is not used: the remaining keys go to the sign-in screen after the switch (a test artifact). — session-control and browser-events are plain Playwright + the existing roundai.test-only session hook.

NOT exercised: one session end across all fields (the scenario's 'when'); on main the app shows sign-in at the next server call (a tab switch is enough), so a physician cannot reach a second field after the session ends. The patch's oracleNote recording this scope change is PROPOSED for Quinn / Daniela's approval, not merged. History (tails typed key by key until 17:12 JST): efs16 4 attempts timed out on the loaded stack; efs16b + efs16c 7 attempts: 1 passed, 3 with tails missing after sign-in (NH visit x2, Hospital all three x1), 3 timeouts. Key-by-key typing is not a valid driver here: the app switches to sign-in at the first refused autosave and the remaining keys go to the sign-in screen, so only the text that was in the field at the switch exists to restore (a test artifact, not a loss).
